title: Extracellular vesicle and particle isolation from human and murine cell lines, tissues, and bodily fluids
protocol: Perform serial centrifugation and ultracentrifugation steps to isolate EVPs from conditioned cell culture media.
Harvest culture media and remove cells, debris, apoptotic bodies, and contaminants through serial centrifugation.
Centrifuge sample at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet cells and debris.
Collect the supernatant without disturbing the cell/debris pellet.
Pipette off the supernatant carefully into a new container/tube.
Keep supernatants on ice between isolation steps.
Centrifuge sample at 3,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C to remove additional cell debris contaminants before short-term storage or freezing.
Store conditioned media supernatants at -80°C for long-term storage or at 4°C for short-term (<24 h) storage before ultracentrifugation.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 12,000 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C to remove apoptotic bodies and aggregates and larger vesicles.
Collect the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Transfer the supernatant to a new/clean ultracentrifuge tube by pipetting, leaving a small volume behind to avoid contamination from the pellet.
Wash newly purchased ultracentrifugation tubes with soap and water.
Rinse the tubes extensively in ddH2O before first use.
Thoroughly wash the tubes in soap and hot water while scrubbing with a brush.
Rinse the tubes thoroughly with tap water to remove any traces of soap.
Perform additional rinses with ddH2O.
Autoclave the tubes if required for in vitro or in vivo work, but this shortens tube life.
Avoid disturbing the pellet during centrifugation steps.
Leave a minimal amount of media above the pellet to avoid dissociating it.
Centrifuge supernatant at 100,000 × g for 70 min at 10°C in a fixed-angle rotor in a Beckman Coulter ultracentrifuge.
Carefully decant the supernatant after centrifugation.
Mark an area on the bottom of the tube where the pellet is expected to form.
Re-suspend the EVP pellet in a small volume of PBS (0.5–1 mL depending on tube size) by pipetting and flushing the marked area of the lower side of the ultracentrifuge tube.
Avoid generating bubbles during re-suspension.
Discard the supernatant by decanting or carefully pipetting without disturbing the pellet.
Keep the tip of the pipet on the side of the tube opposite from the pellet if pipetting off the supernatant.
Pour the supernatant off the side of the tube opposite the pellet and use one quick, careful motion to invert the tube if decanting.
Store supernatant if interested in EVP-depleted media for measurement of other secreted factors such as cytokines.
Leave the pellet untouched after removing the supernatant and place the inverted tube in a rack for 1–3 min.
Remove drops of liquid from tube walls by vacuum aspiration or using a Kimwipe if necessary.
Re-suspend the pellet in 500 μL of cold PBS by pipetting and flushing the marked area at the bottom of the ultracentrifugation tube.
Transfer the re-suspended pellet to a new ultracentrifuge tube.
Add 3 mL, 20 mL, or 44 mL of cold PBS depending on the size of the ultracentrifuge tube used.
Centrifuge the re-suspended pellet at 100,000 × g for 70 min at 10°C to collect the washed EVP pellet.
Discard the PBS supernatant by decanting.
Remove all liquid from the inverted tube gently to avoid backflow.
Re-suspend the EVP pellet in 100 μL of cold PBS.
Store the re-suspended sample at -80°C.
Reserve 10 μL aliquots for downstream quantification and characterization, such as protein quantification, NTA, and EM.
Adjust the final re-suspension volume between 50 μL and 500 μL based on EVP yield.
Empirically establish the EVP yield for each cell type.
Re-suspend the EVP pellet directly in cell lysis buffer for downstream RNA or protein applications if desired.
Perform an additional centrifugation at 12,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C to remove potential aggregates/precipitates before downstream analysis.
Reconstitute fresh human tumor tissues and peritumoral adjacent tissues with ice-cold PBS.
Transfer tissues on ice to a class II biosafety cabinet within 30 minutes of surgery.
Collect the tumor tissue and adjacent tissue in ice-cold PBS at the time of surgery.
Work quickly or in PBS to avoid drying out tissue and decreasing EVP yield.
Wash tissues in cold PBS × 3.
Quickly cut the tissues into 2 mm³-sized pieces.
Rinse tissue pieces again in PBS before plating if needed to remove debris and/or blood.
Allow tissue pieces to adhere to the plastic dishes for a few minutes before adding media.
Pipette media slowly against the side of the dish to avoid disturbing the tissue pieces.
Ensure enough media is added to cover the tissue pieces and try to minimize detachment from the plate.
Transfer plates to 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Collect culture media after 16–18 h without disturbing tissue explants.
Keep collected media on ice.
Centrifuge the culture media at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant to a new tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 3,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant to a new tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 500 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge the supernatant again at 3,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge the supernatant once more at 12,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Isolate extracellular vesicles by ultracentrifugation at 100,000 × g for 70 min at 10°C.
Re-suspend the EVP pellet in 2.5 mL of PBS if further purification is desired.
Tilt the tube to 45° and slowly overlay onto a 0.5 mL sucrose/deuterium oxide cushion layer.
Centrifuge at 100,000 × g for 70 min at 10°C.
Aspirate the lower fraction using an 18 G needle and 3 ml syringe.
Ensure not to disturb the layers or eventual pellet when aspirating.
Collect a volume similar to the amount of sucrose/deuterium oxide mixture added.
Re-suspend EVP pellet in 3 mL of PBS.
Perform ultracentrifugation at 100,000 × g for 70 minutes at 10°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Re-suspend collected EVP pellet in 100 μL of PBS.
Store the re-suspended pellet at -80°C.
Save 10 μL aliquots for protein quantification, NTA, and EM.
Centrifuge the EDTA tube containing the blood at 500 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Check that the plasma layer is yellow and clear, indicating no red blood cell lysis.
If needed, confirm absence of hemolysis by spectrophotometric measurement at 414 nm.
Exclude samples with a cloudy appearance due to high lipid content.
For viscous samples like bile or pancreatic duct fluid, add ice-cold PBS at a ratio of 1:1.
Homogenize the mixture by repeated pipetting.
Do not disturb the pellet after each centrifugation step.
Collect most of the plasma while leaving a small residual volume above the pellet.
Handle a maximum of 10 plasma samples at one time.
Pipette the top layer without touching the interphase layer and transfer into a new tube.
Centrifuge the plasma at 3,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Collect the plasma and discard the platelet-rich pellet if not needed.
Pause point: The plasma can be frozen at -80°C for long-term storage.
Centrifuge the plasma at 12,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C in either a tabletop microcentrifuge or an ultracentrifuge.
Filter the cleared post-12,000 × g plasma supernatant through a 1.2 μm membrane (optional).
Perform a 12,000 × g spin before ultracentrifugation steps.
Save 100 μL aliquots of cleared plasma for EVP quantification and characterization.
Isolate extracellular vesicles by ultracentrifugation.
Transfer the plasma supernatant to an ultracentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge sample at 100,000 × g for 70 minutes at 10°C in a fixed angle rotor.
Decant or carefully pipette off the plasma, leaving the pellet untouched.
Place the inverted tube in a tube rack to drain and avoid liquid backflow.
Note the volume of plasma for calculating extracellular vesicle numbers and protein per milliliter plasma.
Resuspend the extracellular vesicle pellet in 500 μL of ice-cold PBS.
Transfer the resuspended pellet to a second ultracentrifuge tube.
Add 3.5 mL of PBS to wash the pellet.
Centrifuge the sample at 100,000 × g for 70 minutes at 10°C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting and ensure there is no liquid backflow onto the pellet.
Re-suspend the pellet in 100 μL of PBS.
Store the re-suspended sample at −80°C.
Save aliquots for protein quantification, NTA, and EM to avoid freeze-thaw cycles.
Pre-clear the EVP suspension by centrifuging at 12,000 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant into a pre-chilled screw cap vial.
Place the sample vial into the designated position in the pre-chilled autosampler.
Determine empirically that 40–100 μg of EVP protein is required for AF4 processing.
Ensure a sample concentration range of 0.4–1 μg/μL is used for AF4 due to the size of the sample injection loop.
Set parameters for data collection in Astra 6: MALS data collection interval at 1 s and QELS interval at 2 s; total data collection time set to 60 min.
Save the file and click “RUN.”
Data collection automatically starts once triggered by the autosampler sample loading.
Use Chemstation software with an integrated Eclipse module to operate the AF4.
Program a new method or load the desired method from the method library.
Set forward channel flow at 1 mL/min for elution for 2 minutes, Vx at 0.5 mL/min.
Continue focus for 1 minute at Vx of 0.5 mL/min.
Proceed with focus plus injection for 2 minutes, Vx at 0.5 mL/min and injection flow at 0.2 mL/min.
Initiate elution for 45 minutes with a linear gradient decreasing from 0.5 to 0 mL/min.
Elute for an additional 5 minutes at Vx of 0 mL/min.
Collect fractions by time slice (0.5 min/fraction) using the fraction collector module.
Set input sample volume in the autosampler module to <=100 μL.
Run a single sample and start data collection with Astra 6 once loading is complete.
Switch off all lasers and thermostats for both autosamplers and fraction collector after processing samples for the day.
Clean the flow cell of the Dawn Heleos II detector using COMET for about 30 minutes.
Change buffer to water and run Night Rinse mode for approximately 16-18 hours for long-term storage.
Run a blank control using PBS with the same running method as the EVP samples.
Evaluate instrument performance using the background noise level and baseline drifting from the blank control.
Fractionate samples more than 100 μg or larger than 100 μL sequentially via AF4 using the same running method.
Pool fractions according to their hydrodynamic sizes after sequential fractionation.
Seal collected fraction plates with adhesive tapes and keep them on ice at 4°C for up to 2–3 days if not immediately proceeding.
Concentrate and characterize each EVP fraction using Astra 6 software.
Adjust the baseline of data collected from each monitor in the experiment within Astra 6.
Save the changes made to the baselines in Astra 6.
Open a new window of EASI Graph in Astra 6.
Plot the hydrodynamic radius (Rh) of particles vs Time.
Pre-wet the Millipore centrifugal filter columns with Ultracel-30 membrane (30 kDa cutoff) with cold PBS and spin in tabletop clinical centrifuge at 3,700 × g at 4°C for 5 min.
Discard the residual liquid in the filter unit and flow-through in the collection tube.
Transfer the pooled fractions into the filter column (top part).
Spin at 3,700 × g at 4°C for 7–8 min.
Discard the flow-through but keep the samples retained in upper chamber of the filter column.
Repeat step 34 until each pooled set is concentrated to the desired volume using a single filter column.
Mix the concentrated samples gently and transfer to Eppendorf tubes on ice.
Add an additional volume of PBS to rinse the filter column and combine with the sample.
Record the volume of the final product.
Remove an aliquot for BCA assay and/or NTA analysis to determine protein concentration and/or particle concentration.
Save a small aliquot (~1 μg) to verify particle integrity and morphology by TEM.
Use the EVP subsets immediately for downstream analysis or keep on ice for short-term storage.
Keep aliquots frozen at -80°C for long-term storage.

Examine the morphology of EVPs present in representative individual fractions by TEM before pooling fractions together for further processing and analysis if samples are from a specific type of source material that has never been analyzed previously by AF4.
Concentrate a large volume of pooled fractions using ultracentrifugation at 100,000 × g at 10°C for 70 min as an alternative approach.
Resuspend the pelleted EVP subsets in the desired volume of PBS or other types of solution required by downstream analysis.
